metadata.title: Create sftp ingestion for LA HIE

issue_payload.body:
_[Release PRs:]_

Issues:

- https://linear.app/metriport/issue/ENG-968

### Dependencies
- https://github.com/metriport/metriport-internal/pull/3252

### Description
Add SFTP ingestion from LaHie.
Using this flow:
- Sync files from LaHie to S3 using SFTP
- Decrypt data using PGP
- Convert data from PSV to Hl7
- Send data to webhook sender

Refactor mllp-server so that webhook sender handles timezones instead of the mllp server.

### Testing
- Local:
  - [x] Run test cases for MSH, EVN, PID, PV1, PV2, DG1
  - [x] Use the script to ingest the test data given to me from local machine:
           - Make sure data got correctly decrypted and stored in S3.
           - Make sure data got sent to webhook.
           - Check s3 conversion bucket for FHIR resources.
           - Make sure the FHIR resources make sense.
 - [x] Use script to send an mllp message with a different timezone (Chicago) and see if it turns into UTC properly
- Staging:
  - [x] Run test cases for MSH, EVN, PID, PV1, PV2, DG1
  - [ ] Use the script to ingest whatever Lahie has in their test directory.
  - [ ] Test MLLP server + webhook sender??
 - Production:
   - [ ] Run test cases for MSH, EVN, PID, PV1, PV2, DG1
   - [ ] Use the script to ingest the Lahie data asap and monitor
          
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * LAHIE HL7v2 SFTP ingestion (direct and cloud) with scheduled Lambda, local CLI, and environment-aware factory.

* **Improvements**
  * Centralized replica syncing with explicit error handling and GPG decryption support.
  * PSV→HL7 conversion pipeline with validation/normalization and timezone-aware handling.
  * Simplified webhook payloads and standardized timestamps/acknowledgements.

* **Infrastructure**
  * New S3 bucket, LAHIE SFTP config and secrets, and HIE config dictionary injected into Lambdas.

* **Tests**
  * Comprehensive PSV→HL7 conversion test suite.

* **Chores**
  * Added runtime dependencies (openpgp, ip-cidr).

```diff
@@
-main();
+void main().catch(err => {
+  // keep single-line logs per guidelines
+  console.error("LaHie local run failed:", err);
+  process.exit(1);
+});
```

Also add explicit return type. ```diff - static async create(isLocal?: boolean): Promise { + static async create(isLocal?: boolean): Promise { const host = Config.getLaHieIngestionHost(); const port = Config.getLaHieIngestionPort(); const username = Config.getLaHieIngestionUsername(); - const password = isLocal ? this.LOCAL_PASSWORD : await this.getLaHiePassword(); + const password = await this.getLaHiePassword(); const replica = isLocal ? this.getLocalReplica() : this.getLaHieReplica(); return new LaHieSftpClient( { host, port, username, password, }, replica ); } ``` --- `51-53`: **Local replica path should come from Config, not a class constant** Prevents personal paths in source and centralizes configuration. ```diff static getLocalReplica(): ReplicaConfig { - return { type: "local", path: this.LOCAL_PATH }; issue_payload.body: Ref: #960 ### Dependencies - Upstream: https://github.com/metriport/metriport-internal/pull/1197 ### Description - Added a new public route `GET to get a presigned URL for document upload and creates a DocRef - Added a lambda that triggers upon s3 file upload in a designated bucket and sends a request to an internal route - Added a new internal route `POST /internal/docs/doc-ref` that generates and stores a DocRef to the newly uploaded file ### Screenshots ### Additional Context As these DocRefs might be left in the drafted state (if file upload/post-processing fails), it's a good idea to be able to filter those out when querying for DocRefs - [related issue](https://github.com/metriport/metriport-internal/issues/1200). ### Release Plan - [ ] Merge upstream PR - [ ] Merge this - [ ] Release NPM pkg

issue_payload.body:
This is a draft for the initial implementation of the Surescripts client. This combines the initial testing scripts and validation work from the [ENG-194 branch](https://github.com/metriport/metriport/tree/eng-194-surescripts-v0-design-doc) into a proper Surescripts client, with full unit testing and robust SFTP error handling.

Issues:

- https://linear.app/metriport/issue/ENG-306
- https://linear.app/metriport/issue/ENG-313 (CDK related changes) 

### Dependencies

- Upstream: None
- Downstream: None

### Description

This creates a `SurescriptsSftpClient` class, which provides an abstraction layer for producing messages in the Surescripts pipe-delimited format for SFTP bulk transfers.

### Testing

- **Local**: You **should not test Surescripts locally**. Surescripts has white-listed the specific IP addresses associated with outbound traffic from our staging VPC for their SFTP sandbox, and production IP addresses for their production SFTP endpoint. Furthermore, the credentials for authenticating with Surescripts should be loaded from AWS Secrets Manager only.

- **Staging**:
There are commands and tests located within the `sftp` directory, as well as the `surescripts` extension of the base `SftpClient` implementation. These must be executed from a compute resource (Lambda, EC2) within the staging VPC. The simplest way to test the client against the Surescripts SFTP sandbox is:

1. connect by VPN to staging
2. use the SSH key stored in 1PW under "Surescripts Staging Instance" to ssh into the machine
3. run the test command within the `metriport` directory (a semi-initialized git clone of this repository)
4. check the corresponding `metriport-surescripts-replica-staging` bucket to ensure that generated files are present and meet manual validation
5. Run the automated scripts in the `external/sftp` directory (`npx jest -- external/sftp`)

- **Production**:
[ TODO ]

### Release Plan

This client implementation currently only interacts with the `metriport-surescripts-replica-[staging|production]` buckets, and provides an initial implementation for the associated Lambda functions from the `SurescriptsNestedStack` in the CDK.

- [ ] Upstream dependencies are met/released

## Walkthrough

This update introduces a comprehensive Surescripts integration, adding core SFTP client infrastructure, Surescripts-specific file generation and parsing, and robust Lambda and CLI tooling for sending and receiving patient and batch requests. It includes extensive schema validation, type-safe code mappings, file name utilities, and replica storage support. The infrastructure and configuration are refactored to support new Lambda functions and queues, with corresponding environment variable and secret management. Numerous test suites and test artifacts are added to ensure correctness of file parsing, ID generation, and demographic handling.

## Changes

| File(s) / Path(s)                                                                                  | Change Summary |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------|
| `packages/core/src/external/sftp/client.ts`, `compression.ts`, `types.ts`, `replica/local.ts`, `replica/s3.ts` | Introduced a robust SFTP client with support for connection management, gzip compression, error handling, and replica storage (S3/local), along with supporting types and replica implementations. |
| `packages/core/src/external/sftp/command/sftp-action/…`                                            | Added a typed SFTP action framework with direct and cloud (Lambda) handlers, a factory, and comprehensive action/result typing. |
| `packages/core/src/external/surescripts/client.ts`, `file-generator.ts`, `file-names.ts`, `id-generator.ts`, `data-mapper.ts`, `codes.ts`, `constants.ts`, `types.ts` | Added Surescripts SFTP client, file generation/parsing utilities, ID generator, code mappings, constants, and domain types for Surescripts integration. |
| `packages/core/src/external/surescripts/schema/…`                                                  | Added Zod schemas and parsing/serialization logic for Surescripts patient load, verification, and flat file response files, including shared field converters. |
| `packages/core/src/external/surescripts/command/…`                                                 | Introduced command handler interfaces and implementations (direct/cloud) for sending/receiving patient/batch requests, verifications, and responses, with environment-based factories. |
| `packages/core/src/external/surescripts/api/…`                                                     | Added API helpers for fetching customer, facility, and patient data, including retry logic and schema validation. |
| `packages/shared/src/domain/patient.ts`, `customer.ts`                                             | Added Zod schemas and types for Patient and Customer data. |
| `packages/shared/src/common/date.ts`, `demographics.ts`                                            | Added date/time formatting utilities and name/gender parsing/mapping functions. |
| `packages/shared/src/interface/external/surescripts/…`                                             | Added DEA schedule code constants/types and re-exported them from the Surescripts interface. |
| `packages/core/src/external/surescripts/__tests__/…`, `sftp/__tests__/client.test.ts`, `shared/__tests__/…` | Added extensive test suites for Surescripts file parsing, ID generation, file name utilities, SFTP client, demographics, and date utilities, along with test artifacts. |
| `packages/lambdas/src/surescripts/…`                                                               | Added/updated Lambda handlers for Surescripts send/receive/verify actions, batch requests, and SFTP actions, using new client and handler implementations. |
| `packages/lambdas/src/surescripts/shared.ts`                                                       | Added utility to create Surescripts SFTP client with secret management. |
| `packages/infra/lib/surescripts/surescripts-stack.ts`, `types.ts`, `api-stack.ts`, `api-stack/api-service.ts` | Refactored Surescripts infrastructure: replaced/renamed Lambdas and queues, unified concurrency/timeouts, added assets/queue mapping, and updated environment variable and secret management. |
| `packages/core/src/external/surescripts/__tests__/artifacts/…`                                     | Added test artifact files for various Surescripts file scenarios. |
| `packages/utils/src/surescripts/…`                                                                 | Introduced CLI commands for SFTP actions, sending/receiving patient/batch requests, verification, and response handling, including CSV parsing for batch requests. |
| `packages/utils/.env.example`, `.env.test`, `package.json`                                         | Added Surescripts-related environment variable placeholders, removed trailing newline, and added a CLI script. |

## Sequence Diagram(s)

### Surescripts Patient Request (Direct Lambda/CLI)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User/Trigger
    participant Lambda/CLI
    participant SurescriptsSftpClient
    participant SFTP Server
    participant (Optional) S3 Replica

    User/Trigger->>Lambda/CLI: Provide cxId, facilityId, patientId
    Lambda/CLI->>SurescriptsSftpClient: sendPatientRequest(requestData)
    SurescriptsSftpClient->>SFTP Server: Connect & upload request file
    SurescriptsSftpClient-->>Lambda/CLI: Return transmissionId
```

### Surescripts Batch Request (Direct Lambda/CLI)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User/Trigger
    participant Lambda/CLI
    participant SurescriptsSftpClient
    participant SFTP Server
    participant (Optional) S3 Replica

    User/Trigger->>Lambda/CLI: Provide cxId, facilityId, patientIds/CSV
    Lambda/CLI->>SurescriptsSftpClient: sendBatchRequest(requestData)
    SurescriptsSftpClient->>SFTP Server: Connect & upload batch file
    SurescriptsSftpClient-->>Lambda/CLI: Return transmissionId, requestedPatientIds
```

### Surescripts Receive Response (Direct Lambda/CLI)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User/Trigger
    participant Lambda/CLI
    participant SurescriptsSftpClient
    participant (Optional) S3 Replica
    participant SFTP Server

    User/Trigger->>Lambda/CLI: Provide transmissionId, populationId
    Lambda/CLI->>SurescriptsSftpClient: receiveResponse(identifier)
    alt Replica enabled and file exists
        SurescriptsSftpClient->>S3 Replica: Read response file
    else
        SurescriptsSftpClient->>SFTP Server: Download response file
        SurescriptsSftpClient->>S3 Replica: Write file to replica
    end
    SurescriptsSftpClient-->>Lambda/CLI: Return file content
```

### SFTP Action (Cloud Handler)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User/Trigger
    participant SftpActionCloud
    participant AWS Lambda (SFTP Handler)
    participant SFTP Server

    User/Trigger->>SftpActionCloud: executeAction(action)
    SftpActionCloud->>AWS Lambda: Invoke Lambda with action
    AWS Lambda->>SFTP Server: Perform SFTP operation
    AWS Lambda-->>SftpActionCloud: Return result/error
    SftpActionCloud-->>User/Trigger: Return result/error
```

### Infrastructure: Surescripts Lambda Setup

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant CDK Stack
    participant SurescriptsStack
    participant Lambda
    participant SQS Queue

    CDK Stack->>SurescriptsStack: Instantiate with config
    SurescriptsStack->>Lambda: Create Lambda(s) with env vars & secrets
    SurescriptsStack->>SQS Queue: Create SQS queue(s) as needed
    SurescriptsStack->>Lambda: Attach queue(s) and permissions
    SurescriptsStack-->>CDK Stack: Expose assets (lambdas, queues)
```

discussion_timeline.body:
[packages/core/src/external/sftp/id-generator.ts] The rationale for this is that we get 10 bytes to provide a unique transaction ID, and this method (which I've tested with the SS sandbox) does work for producing something that might be described as a "10 byte UUID v7". That is, the generated ID is guaranteed to be

- unique, even if generated in the same millisecond (there are 2 bytes of randomness after the 8 bytes of timestamp)
- allowed by Surescripts' ASCII range for IDs, which is 32 - 126 (see `LEXICON`)
- lexicographically sortable (i.e. an ID which was issued later will always be alphabetically after an ID which was issued sooner, and vice versa)
- synchronous (vs having to add an asynchronous DB request)

discussion_timeline.body:
[packages/core/src/external/sftp/client.ts] One difference from the implementation last week is that the extra SSH listeners to listen for errors that are not thrown into a try-catch statement are only attached once. This is due to guidance from the `ssh2-sftp-client` documentation:

> Due to an issue with ECONNRESET error signals when connecting to Windows based SFTP servers, it is not possible to remove the error handler in the end() method. This means that if you re-use the SftpClient object for multiple connections e.g. calling connect(), then end(), then connect() etc, you run the risk of multiple error handlers being added to the SftpClient object. After 11 handlers have been added, Node will generate a possible memory leak warning.

[packages/core/src/external/sftp/api/shared.ts] _⚠️ Potential issue_

**Fix the debug logging implementation.**

The current debug logging call is incorrect:

```typescript
debug(`${url} resp: `, () => JSON.stringify(response.data));
```

This passes a function as the second parameter to `debug`, but `console.log` (which `debug` is typed as) doesn't accept a function parameter. The function won't be executed, and you'll likely see `[Function]` in the logs instead of the actual data.



Apply this fix:

```diff
- debug(`${url} resp: `, () => JSON.stringify(response.data));
+ debug(`${url} resp: `, JSON.stringify(response.data));
```

Or if you want to support lazy evaluation for performance:

```diff
- debug(`${url} resp: `, () => JSON.stringify(response.data));
+ debug(`${url} resp: ${JSON.stringify(response.data)}`);
```

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Added support for scheduling, running, failing, and cancelling patient jobs, including new endpoints for managing job lifecycle and runtime data.
  - Introduced job filtering and retrieval by various parameters such as status, scheduled dates, and identifiers.
  - Implemented infrastructure for patient job processing using AWS Lambda and SQS, with robust error handling and monitoring.
  - Added runtime data management for patient jobs, allowing runtime data to be fetched and updated.

  - Integrated patient job queue permissions and environment variables into API service deployment.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved validation for date and status parameters in job-related endpoints.

- **Chores**
  - Refactored and reorganized code to support new job features and infrastructure, including type and schema updates.

## Walkthrough

This update introduces a comprehensive patient job scheduling and execution framework. It adds new fields to the patient job model, enables job scheduling, cancellation, and failure, and provides infrastructure for running jobs via SQS and Lambda. The API surface is expanded with endpoints for job management, and supporting types, handlers, and infrastructure stacks are implemented.

## Changes

| File(s) / Path(s)                                                                                       | Change Summary |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------|
| `packages/api/src/command/job/patient/create.ts`, `get.ts`, `scheduler/start-jobs.ts`, `status/cancel.ts`, `status/complete.ts`, `status/fail.ts`, `status/initialize.ts`, `update/set-entry-status.ts`, `update/update-runtime-data.ts`, `update/update-total.ts` | Refactored and expanded patient job command handlers: new fields, status transitions (cancel/fail), runtime data update, job scheduling, and parameter type updates. |
| `packages/api/src/command/job/shared.ts`                                                                | Removed shared job parameter/response types (now inlined or moved). |
| `packages/api/src/external/ehr/shared/job/bundle/create-resource-diff-bundles/run-job.ts`, `start-job.ts`, `get-job-payload.ts`, `utils/job.ts` | Added/updated job execution logic, run URL utilities, and refactored job creation to remove concurrency checks. |
| `packages/api/src/models/patient-job.ts`, `packages/shared/src/domain/job/patient-job.ts`               | Extended patient job model/type with `runUrl`, `scheduledAt`, `cancelledAt`, `failedAt`, `runtimeData`; added raw column mapping. |
| `packages/api/src/routes/internal/medical/patient-job.ts`, `ehr/job.ts`, `ehr/index.ts`, `ehr/patient.ts` | Added/updated API endpoints for job management: scheduling, status transitions, runtime data, and job execution. |
| `packages/api/src/sequelize/migrations/2025-06-17_00_alter-patient-job-add-scheduled-at.ts`             | Migration: added new columns to the patient job table and a status index. |
| `packages/api/src/shared/date.ts`, `packages/shared/src/common/date.ts`                                 | Added ISO date-time validation and utility for date parsing/validation. |
| `packages/core/src/command/job/patient/api/complete-job.ts`, `initialize-job.ts`, `set-entry-status.ts`, `update-job-total.ts` | Refactored logging/response validation and updated endpoint paths. |
| `packages/core/src/command/job/patient/api/get-jobs.ts`, `run-job.ts`, `update-job-runtime-data.ts`, `shared.ts` | Added API calls for job listing, execution, runtime data update, and shared parameter types. |
| `packages/core/src/command/job/patient/command/run-job/run-job-cloud.ts`, `run-job-direct.ts`, `run-job-factory.ts`, `run-job.ts` | Implemented job runner handlers (direct/cloud), factory, and request types for job execution. |
| `packages/core/src/external/ehr/api/job/shared.ts`                                                      | Removed obsolete shared job parameter type. |
| `packages/core/src/external/ehr/job/create-resource-diff-bundles/steps/compute/ehr-compute-resource-diff-bundles-cloud.ts`, `steps/compute/ehr-compute-resource-diff-bundles.ts`, `steps/refresh/ehr-refresh-ehr-bundles-cloud.ts`, `steps/refresh/ehr-refresh-ehr-bundles.ts` | Updated import paths for shared utilities/types. |

## Sequence Diagram(s)

### Patient Job Scheduling and Execution Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant API
    participant DB as PatientJob DB
    participant SQS as SQS Queue
    participant Lambda as RunJob Lambda

    Client->>API: POST /internal/patient/job (create job with runUrl, scheduledAt)
    API->>DB: Insert patient job (with runUrl, scheduledAt)
    alt scheduledAt is not set (immediate run)
        API->>SQS: Enqueue job (id, cxId, runUrl)
    end
    SQS->>Lambda: Trigger event (job message)
    Lambda->>API: POST runUrl (with jobId, cxId)
    API->>DB: Update job status (processing/completed/failed)
```

### Job Status Transition (Cancel/Fail)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant API
    participant DB as PatientJob DB

    Client->>API: POST /internal/patient/job/:jobId/cancel or /fail
    API->>DB: Update job status (cancelled or failed), set cancelledAt/failedAt
    API-->>Client: 200 OK (updated job)
```

### Scheduled Job Runner

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Scheduler
    participant API
    participant DB as PatientJob DB
    participant SQS as SQS Queue

    Scheduler->>API: POST /internal/patient/job/scheduler/start
    API->>DB: Query jobs (status=waiting, scheduledBefore=now)
    loop For each job with runUrl
        API->>SQS: Enqueue job (id, cxId, runUrl)
    end
```

## Possibly related PRs

- [metriport/metriport#3714](https://github.com/metriport/metriport/pull/3714): Introduced the original `createPatientJob` function with concurrency checks. The current changes modify this function by removing concurrency checks and adding synchronous job execution via `runUrl`.
- [metriport/metriport#3682](https://github.com/metriport/metriport/pull/3682): Also introduced the original `createPatientJob` with concurrency logic, which is now refactored in this update to support immediate execution and new parameters.

packages/core/src/command/job/patient/api/set-entry-status.ts (1)
`31-38`: _🛠️ Refactor suggestion_ **Reduce repetition – extract a tiny helper** `completeJob`, `initializeJob`, `updateJobTotal`, and `setJobEntryStatus` all duplicate: - `axios.create({ baseURL })` - retry wrapper - `logAxiosResponse` A shared utility such as `postInternalJobEndpoint({ path, params })` would cut ~30 lines per file and ensure consistent error handling.
packages/api/src/command/job/patient/update/update-total.ts (1)
`22-29`: _⚠️ Potential issue_ **Missing guard against updating a running job – spec/doc mismatch** The JSDoc advertises: > “throws BadRequestError if the job total is already set and the job is running.” The implementation only validates `total < 1`; it never checks whether a) `job.total` is already set, or b) the job is currently running. That means an in-flight job can have its counters silently reset, breaking every consumer that relies on the invariants `(successful + failed ≤ total)`. Suggested minimal fix: ```diff @@ -const jobModel = await getPatientJobModelOrFail({ jobId, cxId }); +const jobModel = await getPatientJobModelOrFail({ jobId, cxId }); +const job = jobModel.dataValues; + +// Prevent mutating totals for jobs that are already in progress or completed +if (job.total !== null && ["running", "queued"].includes(job.status)) { + throw new BadRequestError( + `Cannot update total for a job in status ${job.status}` + ); +} ``` Optionally refuse updates when `job.total` is already > 0 regardless of status if that better matches business rules.
packages/shared/src/domain/job/job-status.ts (1)
`18-20`: _🛠️ Refactor suggestion_ **`isJobDone` omits `cancelled`** In many systems a cancelled job is considered terminal. If callers rely on `isJobDone`, they may endlessly poll a cancelled job. ```diff -export function isJobDone(status: JobStatus): boolean { - return status === "completed" || status === "failed"; +export function isJobDone(status: JobStatus): boolean { + return status === "completed" || status === "failed" || status === "cancelled"; } ```

packages/core/src/command/job/patient/api/initialize-job.ts (1)

`21-29`: **Consistent param handling & logging concerns (see prior comments)** Same points as in `completeJob`/`initializeJob`: 1. Replace manual query construction with Axios `params`. 2. Re-evaluate logging of full `response.data` for PHI.
🧹 Nitpick comments (25)
packages/core/src/command/job/patient/api/complete-job.ts (1)
`17-24`: **Avoid manual query-string assembly – leverage Axios `params` for correctness & readability** Manually concatenating `?${queryParams.toString()}` works but is easy to break (e.g., double `?`, forgotten encoding, trailing `&`). Axios already handles this via its `params` option: ```diff -const queryParams = new URLSearchParams({ cxId }); -const completeJobUrl = `/internal/patient/job/${jobId}/complete?${queryParams.toString()}`; -... -const response = await executeWithNetworkRetries(async () => { - return api.post(completeJobUrl); -}); +const completeJobUrl = `/internal/patient/job/${jobId}/complete`; +... +const response = await executeWithNetworkRetries(async () => { + return api.post(completeJobUrl, undefined, { params: { cxId } }); +}); ``` Benefits: centralised encoding, reduced string-bashing, clearer intent.
packages/api/src/command/job/patient/status/initialize.ts (1)
`24-34`: **Minor JSDoc mismatch – parameter name** The code uses `cxId`, but the docstring line still says “customer ID”. Consider clarifying (`cxId - The customer (CX) ID`). Small but keeps docs accurate.
packages/api/src/routes/internal/medical/patient-jobs/index.ts (1)
`6-8`: **Router export is fine – consider using a named export for consistency** Most route modules in the code-base appear to use `export default` but a few expose a named constant. Mixing the two styles can bite during refactors (e.g., when converting to ESM or re-exporting barrels). If there is no established convention yet, consider switching to ```diff -const router = Router(); -... -export default router; +export const router = Router(); +... ``` and importing it with `import { router as patientJobsRouter } from "./ehr"` to keep everything explicit. No functional changes required – this is purely a consistency nit.
packages/api/src/shared/config.ts (1)
`122-125`: **Wrapper now just forwards to core – consider de-duplicating sooner** `getDBCreds` is now a pure pass-through to `CoreConfig.getDBCreds()`. If nothing inside `api` calls the core implementation directly, we are keeping two public APIs that must stay in sync. ```diff /** @deprecated Use core's version of Config instead */ static getDBCreds(): string { - return CoreConfig.getDBCreds(); + // TODO: remove once callers migrate to CoreConfig + return CoreConfig.getDBCreds(); } ``` Follow-up: 1. Search for `Config.getDBCreds(` usages and migrate them to `CoreConfig`. 2. Delete this wrapper in a subsequent clean-up PR to avoid bit-rot.
packages/infra/lib/shared/secrets.ts (1)
`16-18`: **Nit: keep helper naming consistent with existing API** `buildSecrets` takes a generic `scope: Construct`; the new `buildSecret` takes `nestedStack: Construct`. For symmetry (and to avoid a mental context-switch for callers) prefer the same parameter name & doc comment: ```diff -export function buildSecret(nestedStack: Construct, name: string): secret.ISecret { - return secret.Secret.fromSecretNameV2(nestedStack, name, name); +/** + * Build a single secret reference (sugar over buildSecrets for one entry). + */ +export function buildSecret(scope: Construct, name: string): secret.ISecret { + return secret.Secret.fromSecretNameV2(scope, name, name); } ``` No functional change, purely readability.
packages/core/src/command/job/patient/api/shared.ts (1)
`1-5`: **Export `JobId` to maximise reuse** `JobId` is defined but not exported. Several downstream files may need the exact literal type instead of re-deriving `PatientJob["id"]`. ```diff -type JobId = PatientJob["id"]; +export type JobId = PatientJob["id"]; ``` This avoids duplicating the alias elsewhere and keeps typings DRY.
packages/core/src/command/job/patient/job/start-jobs/steps/run/run-job-direct.ts (1)
`4-12`: **Minor style nit – destructure the argument for readability** Destructuring avoids the `request.` prefix noise and matches the functional-style guideline in the TS coding guide. ```diff - async runJob(request: RunJobRequest): Promise { - await runJob({ - jobId: request.id, - cxId: request.cxId, - jobType: request.jobType, - }); + async runJob({ id: jobId, cxId, jobType }: RunJobRequest): Promise { + await runJob({ jobId, cxId, jobType }); } ```

`14-25`: **Fire-and-forget pattern may terminate execution prematurely** `startJobs` returns as soon as the handler promise is created, not when the jobs are actually fetched/run. In a Lambda or short-lived process this risks the runtime finishing before work completes (even though you attach `.catch`). Consider awaiting (or explicitly documenting that early return is intentional). ```diff -export async function startJobs({...}: StartJobsParams): Promise { +export async function startJobs({...}: StartJobsParams): Promise { const handler = buildGetJobsHandler(); - handler - .getJobs({ runDate, cxId, patientId, jobType, status }) - .catch(processAsyncError("startPatientJobs")); + await handler + .getJobs({ runDate, cxId, patientId, jobType, status }) + .catch(processAsyncError("startPatientJobs")); } ``` If “fire-and-forget” is desired (e.g., for an API `202 Accepted` semantics), mark it with a comment and drop the unnecessary `async` keyword to avoid confusion.
packages/core/src/util/config.ts (1)
`35-38`: **DB credentials accessor returns opaque string – clarify expected format** `getDBCreds()` surfaces a raw `DB_CREDS` string. Call-sites likely need individual fields (host, user, pwd). Consider returning a parsed object (or at least document the expected JSON / connection-string format) to avoid ad-hoc parsing in multiple places.
packages/shared/src/domain/job/patient-job.ts (1)
`24-24`: **Consider using a generic for `runtimeData` for safer downstream usage** `runtimeData: unknown` forces consumers to cast, masking type errors. A generic type parameter keeps flexibility while preserving type-safety: ```diff -export type PatientJob = { +export type PatientJob = { ... - runtimeData: unknown; + runtimeData: TRuntimeData | undefined; } ``` This change is non-breaking if defaulted to `unknown`, but gives callers the option to specify a shape.
packages/api/src/command/job/patient/update/update-runtime-data.ts (2)
`5-14`: **Docstring is misleading & parameter names are out of sync** - The description still says “Updates a patient job's total.” – should be “runtime data.” - `@param runtimeData` does not exist in the signature; the actual key is `data`. Keeping docs accurate prevents downstream confusion. ```diff - * Updates a patient job's total. + * Updates a patient job's runtime data. ... - * @param runtimeData - The runtime data to update. + * @param data - The runtime data payload that will replace the existing value. ``` --- `20-25`: **Return plain object instead of Sequelize instance for cleaner typing** `jobModel.update()` returns a Sequelize instance; returning `dataValues` leaks an internal detail and strips any virtuals/getters. Prefer `updatedJob.get({ plain: true })` (or `toJSON()` on newer Sequelize) to keep a clean POJO and consistent serialization. ```diff -const updatedJob = await jobModel.update(fieldsToUpdate); -return updatedJob.dataValues; +const [updatedJob] = await jobModel.update(fieldsToUpdate, { returning: true }); +return updatedJob.get({ plain: true }); ```

`458-459`: **Grant invoke permission also for `runPatientJobLambda`** The task can invoke `getPatientJobsLambda` but not `runPatientJobLambda`. If direct invocation is ever required (e.g., retries, back-fill scripts) the call will fail with `AccessDenied`. ```diff +jobAssets.runPatientJobLambda.grantInvoke(fargateService.taskDefinition.taskRole); ```

`3-5`: **Consider freezing `RunJobRequest` to avoid accidental mutation** Since the same object may propagate through multiple layers, wrapping the request in `Readonly<...>` (or freezing) enforces immutability per guidelines. ```diff -export type RunJobRequest = Pick & - Partial>; +export type RunJobRequest = Readonly< + Pick & + Partial> +>; ```

`18-25`: **JSDoc path & parameter description don’t match actual route** The JSDoc advertises `POST /internal/medical/patient-job/ehr/...` and says `req.query.jobId`, but the implementation registers `/athenahealth-create-resource-diff-bundles/:jobId/run` (and the Canvas variant) and extracts `jobId` from `req.params`. issue_payload.body:
Issues:

- https://linear.app/metriport/issue/ENG-823

### Dependencies

- Upstream: None
- Downstream: None

### Description

- Adds FHIR conversion for incoming tabular data from Quest Diagnostics. The FHIR conversion logic follows the same pattern as Surescripts for extracting optional values into resource objects.
- Refactoring to ensure consistent usage of the name `patientId` to refer to a *Metriport UUID*, and `externalId` to refer to a 15-character Quest ID  (`/^[A-Z0-9]{15}$/).
- Adds a function to retrieve the Metriport UUID and CX ID from the patient mapping table with a Quest external ID.
- Adds a `PatientMappingDTO` for safe forward-compatible DTO of rows from the patient mapping table

### Testing

- Local
  - [x] `npx jest`
- Staging
  - [x] `npm run quest -- fhir-convert-all`
- Production
  - [ ] `npm run quest -- fhir-convert all`

### Release Plan

- [ ] Merge this

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * API: resolve patient mappings by externalId via a new internal endpoint and client helper.
  * Quest pipeline: end-to-end Quest → FHIR conversion, bundle builders, converters, and persistence.

* **CLI**
  * Added fhir-convert-all and convert-to-csv commands.

* **DTOs / Constants**
  * New patient-mapping DTO, Quest DTOs now include externalId and sourceDocumentKey; many FHIR constants and resource builders added.

* **Refactor**
  * Quest data flow and schemas migrated from patientId to externalId.

* **Chores**
  * Quest scheduled jobs now gated by config.

* **Tests**
  * Tests updated for externalId usage and deterministic timing.

**Prefix S3 key in direct FHIR‐conversion invocation**

The direct handler is currently passing only the bare fileName as the S3 key, but `convertSourceDocumentToFhirBundle` (and in particular its direct implementation in `fhir-converter.ts`) expects the full path under the replica bucket (i.e. including the `source_document/` prefix). Without this,

- `getSourceDocument` will attempt to download from the wrong key and 404.

```diff
+          externalId: sourceDocument.externalId,
+          sourceDocumentKey: `source_document/${sourceDocument.fileName}`,
+        });
```

[packages/core/src/external/quest/fhir/diagnostic-report.ts] _⚠️ Potential issue_

**Bug: DiagnosticReport.code (1..1) is missing; current category usage misapplies profile codes.**

FHIR R4 requires DiagnosticReport.code (1..1). The current implementation sets category (optional) but never sets code. Also, the local/standard profile codes (LPC/SPC) look like report/profile identifiers and should populate DiagnosticReport.code, while category should typically be a service section like LAB (HL7 v2-0074 / DiagnosticServiceSectionCodes).

Apply the following minimal fix: add a proper code and use a standards-based category.

```diff
   return {
     resourceType: "DiagnosticReport",
     id: uuidv7(),

-    subject,

-    ...(specimenReference ? { specimen: specimenReference } : {}),
-    ...(category ? { category } : {}),
```

refs. metriport/metriport-internal#2883

### Description
- Conversion for ADT_A01 and ADT_A03 to FHIR
- Resulting Bundle includes the following:
  - Encounter (with references to all of the above)
  - Condition
  - Practitioner
  - Location
- Added local script to test ADT > FHIR conversion
- Some miscellaneous utils functions throughout the repo to help with this conversion
  - One of these is an update to `metriport/shared`, which will require a new pkg release 

### Testing

- Local
  - [ ] Convert the example ADT messages 

### Release Plan
- [ ] Release NPM packages 
  - `metriport/shared` 
- [ ] Merge this

## Walkthrough

This set of changes introduces a comprehensive HL7v2-to-FHIR conversion pipeline, primarily focused on transforming ADT (Admit, Discharge, Transfer) HL7 messages into FHIR Bundles. The implementation includes new modules for parsing HL7 messages, extracting patient, encounter, practitioner, location, and condition details, and mapping these to structured FHIR resources such as Patient, Encounter, Practitioner, Location, and Condition. Utility functions for HL7 parsing, identifier compression, date handling, and FHIR reference building are added. The control flow for conversion is centralized in a main function that orchestrates the parsing and resource construction, with robust error handling and logging. Supporting scripts and tests are also introduced.

## Changes

| File(s) | Change Summary |
|---------|---------------|
| `.../adt/condition.ts`, `.../adt/encounter.ts`, `.../adt/location.ts`, `.../adt/practitioner.ts`, `.../adt/utils.ts`, `.../adt/mappings.ts` | New modules implementing extraction and conversion of HL7 ADT message segments into FHIR Condition, Encounter, Location, and Practitioner resources, with supporting utility functions and type-safe mappings. |
| `.../hl7v2-to-fhir-conversion/index.ts` | Main conversion entry point: defines conversion parameters, orchestrates HL7 message parsing, resource extraction, FHIR Bundle construction, and error handling for unsupported message types. |
| `.../hl7v2-to-fhir-conversion/shared.ts` | Utility functions for HL7 parsing, identifier compression/decompression, coding system mapping, and HL7 file key construction, with contextual error handling. |
| `.../hl7v2-to-fhir-conversion/msh.ts` | Functions for extracting message type and datetime from HL7 MSH segments, with error handling for missing or malformed segments. |
| `.../external/fhir/shared/bundle.ts` | Adds `BundleWithEntry` type and a function to build FHIR Bundles from resource arrays. |
| `.../external/fhir/shared/references.ts` | Functions and types for building FHIR references for patients, encounter participants, locations, and diagnoses. |
| `.../external/fhir/shared/datetime.ts` | Adds a function to construct FHIR Period objects from date strings, supporting compact date formats. |
| `.../shared/src/common/date.ts`, `.../shared/src/common/__tests__/date.test.ts` | Support for parsing compact date strings and corresponding tests for various date formats. |
| `.../utils/src/hl7v2-notifications/convert-adt-to-fhir-local-example.ts` | Example script for converting local ADT HL7 files into FHIR Bundles, handling input/output and error logging. |
| `.../mllp-server/src/app.ts` | Refactors message type extraction to use a centralized function, simplifying and standardizing message parsing logic. |
| `packages/core/package.json`, `packages/utils/package.json` | Added a development dependency `"@medplum/core": "^3.2.33"` for development purposes. |

## Sequence Diagram(s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant HL7Source as HL7v2 Source
    participant Converter as convertHl7v2MessageToFhir
    participant HL7Parser as HL7 Parser & Utils
    participant FHIRBuilder as FHIR Resource Builders
    participant Bundle as FHIR Bundle

    HL7Source->>Converter: Provide HL7v2 message, cxId, patientId, timestamp
    Converter->>HL7Parser: Parse HL7 message, extract messageType
    HL7Parser-->>Converter: Parsed message, messageType

    alt messageType == "ADT"
        Converter->>FHIRBuilder: Extract Patient, Encounter, Practitioner, Location, Condition
        FHIRBuilder-->>Converter: FHIR Resources
        Converter->>Bundle: Build FHIR Bundle from resources
        Bundle-->>Converter: FHIR Bundle
        Converter->>HL7Source: Return FHIR Bundle
    else messageType unsupported
        Converter->>HL7Source: Throw error (unsupported message type)
    end
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant HL7Parser as HL7 Parser
    participant EncounterBuilder as Encounter Resource Builder
    participant PractitionerBuilder as Practitioner Resource Builder
    participant LocationBuilder as Location Resource Builder
    participant ConditionBuilder as Condition Resource Builder

    HL7Parser->>EncounterBuilder: Provide parsed HL7 ADT message
    EncounterBuilder->>PractitionerBuilder: Extract participant info (attending doctor)
    EncounterBuilder->>LocationBuilder: Extract location info (facility)
    EncounterBuilder->>ConditionBuilder: Extract admit reason/condition
    PractitionerBuilder-->>EncounterBuilder: Practitioner resource, references
    LocationBuilder-->>EncounterBuilder: Location resource, references
    ConditionBuilder-->>EncounterBuilder: Condition resource, references
    EncounterBuilder-->>HL7Parser: Encounter resource with references
```

<!-- walkthrough_end -->

`````suggestion
/**
 * Tries to parse a compact date string in the format YYYYMMDDhhmmss±hhmm
 * (year, month, day, hour, minute, second, timezone)
 * and converts it to ISO 8601 format.
 * @param input The compact date string to parse
 * @returns ISO 8601 formatted date string or undefined if input doesn't match expected format
 */
function tryParseCompactDate(input: string): string | undefined {
  const match = input.match(/^(\d{4})(\d{2})(\d{2})(\d{2})(\d{2})(\d{2})([+-])(\d{2})(\d{2})$/);
  if (!match) return undefined;

  const [, year, month, day, hour, minute, second, sign, tzHour, tzMinute] = match;
  return `${year}-${month}-${day}T${hour}:${minute}:${second}${sign}${tzHour}:${tzMinute}`;
}
`````

## Sequence Diagram(s)

### Discharge Requery Job Creation and Execution

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant HL7Source as HL7 Source
    participant CoreAPI as Core API (HL7 Notification Handler)
    participant API as API Service
    participant SQS as Discharge Requery SQS
    participant Lambda as Discharge Requery Lambda
    participant Patient as Patient Data Services

    HL7Source->>CoreAPI: HL7 "A03" (Discharge) Event
    CoreAPI->>API: POST /internal/patient/monitoring/discharge-requery?cxId&patientId
    API->>API: createDischargeRequeryJob()
    API->>SQS: (Production) Send discharge requery message
    SQS->>Lambda: Trigger Lambda with message
    Lambda->>Patient: processDischargeRequery (direct handler)
    Patient-->>Lambda: Patient query, document query, etc.
    Lambda->>API: updateJobRuntimeData, failJob (as needed)
```

### Discharge Requery Job Completion Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant DocumentWebhook as Document Conversion Webhook
    participant API as API Service
    participant finishDischarge as finishDischargeRequery

    DocumentWebhook->>API: Document conversion status update
    API->>finishDischarge: finishDischargeRequery({cxId, patientId, requestId, status})
    finishDischarge->>API: Mark job complete, update attempts, send analytics
    alt More attempts remain
        finishDischarge->>API: Schedule new discharge requery job
    else No attempts remain
        finishDischarge->>API: Log completion
    end
```

### Discharge Requery Job Deduplication Logic

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant API as API Service
    participant JobStore as Patient Job Store

    API->>JobStore: Query for existing discharge requery jobs
    alt Existing jobs found
        API->>JobStore: Cancel existing jobs (deduplication)
        API->>JobStore: Create new job with earliest scheduledAt and largest attempts
    else No existing jobs
        API->>JobStore: Create new discharge requery job
    end
```
